transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. I guess I came in because... well, lately I keep catching myself thinking that it might just be easier if I didn't wake up. I want to be clear, I haven't made any actual plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But those thoughts just keep popping into my head, and I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
When did you first start having these thoughts about not waking up? Was it something that came on gradually over time, or did it start more suddenly?

Well, it wasn't exactly sudden, but it started after this... big crash I had. That was about three months ago. This low spell has just been hanging on ever since then, and the thoughts kind of crept in as it dragged on.
Before this 'big crash' three months ago, have you ever experienced periods like this where you felt persistently sad or depressed for weeks or months at a time?

Well, maybe I've felt a little down in the past, but nothing exactly like this one. This time... well, after that big burst of energy I was having just wore off, I felt like somebody had completely pulled the plug on me. I would just sit there at the kitchen table, staring at my coffee, feeling totally empty and... I don't know, just ashamed. It's just been like that ever since the energy dropped off.
You mentioned having a 'big burst of energy' before this crash three months ago. During that time when you had all that energy, how long did it last, and what was that period like for you?
Well, that high-energy stretch... it lasted for about three weeks. It started right after I was fired from my job. I just felt like I was completely out of control during that time.
During those three weeks when you had all that energy after being fired, how much sleep were you getting? Did you feel like you needed less sleep than usual, or were you sleeping normally?

Well, I definitely wasn't sleeping normally. There were several nights where I think I only slept maybe two or three hours. But I didn't feel tired at all. I'd get up feeling like I had a full tank, you know? Just completely ready to go and... well, I just felt like I had no reason to slow down.

Before that three-week period of high energy after you were fired, have you ever had other times in your life where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, and felt like you could do anything for days or weeks at a time?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had good days where I felt productive, sure, but nothing like that three-week stretch. That was... that was the first time I ever felt like my engine was just stuck on full throttle like that. So, no, never before that.

Since that three-week high-energy period three months ago, have you had any other times where you felt that same kind of unusual energy, decreased need for sleep, or feeling like you could do anything?

No, not since then. After those three weeks ended, I just crashed, and I've been down in this hole ever since. I haven't felt anything close to that kind of energy again. It's just been the opposite, really.

During those three weeks when you had all that energy and were only sleeping a few hours, did you notice your thoughts were racing or jumping quickly from one thing to another? Or did you feel like you could think more clearly and faster than usual?

Yeah, they were definitely racing. It was like... my thoughts were just jumping so fast from one thing to another. I'd be thinking about my old sales numbers, and then right into new job leads, and then suddenly I'm planning out beer recipes, or getting worked up over old arguments. I couldn't really keep hold of one idea for more than a few seconds before my brain just snapped to the next thing.

Looking back over your entire life before that three-week period three months ago, were there any other times—even shorter ones, maybe just a few days—where you felt unusually happy or excited, needed very little sleep, or felt like you had more energy and confidence than normal?

No, honestly, I really can't think of anything. Like I mentioned earlier, I mean... I've had normal good days, maybe a good weekend if I had a good run of sales at work or something, but never a time where I didn't need sleep or felt unusually confident like that. 

That whole three-week thing was just... completely out of the blue for me. So, no, not even for a few days.

I want to make sure I have this right: before that three-week period three months ago, you're saying you've never had even a shorter episode—maybe just a few days—where you felt unusually happy, or unusually irritable or angry, or where you were much more talkative or outgoing than your normal self?

Yeah, you have it right. I really haven't. I mean, sure, I might get a little annoyed at work if we're swamped or a customer is difficult, but not that unusual anger or irritability you're asking about. And I've never been the type to just be super outgoing or talkative out of nowhere. That three-week stretch was really the first and only time anything like that ever happened to me.
